Efficacious

/ef-ih-KAY-shuhs/ - rhymes with gracious · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Efficacious means producing the intended result, said of remedies and measures rather than of people.

Of every trick the new parents tried, only the car ride was truly efficacious — the baby was asleep before the second stoplight.

Worked Example

Alder Hill had eaten three budgets. Fines slowed nobody; cameras got stolen; the rumble strips wore smooth in a year. Then the city painted the crossing as a floating optical illusion — stripes that seem to hover a foot above the asphalt — and average speeds dropped nine miles per hour in a month. The traffic office, burned three times, ran the numbers twice before saying it aloud: the paint was efficacious.

Efficacious is the exact word because the paint produced the intended result — effective, and proven so. The word is a ruling, not a hope: it arrives after the trial, when the numbers are in. That after-the-numbers flavor is why it clings to remedies, treatments, and measures rather than to people.

How Efficacious Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

effective

effective: the everyday word for working; efficacious is the formal, tested ruling

effectual

effectual: actually achieving the aim; bookish, and usually said of actions

Antonyms

ineffective

ineffective: fails to produce the result

useless

useless: no result worth naming at all

How Strong Is It? — helpful → efficacious → infallible

helpful vs. efficacious

helpful vs. efficacious: A helpful remedy does some good; an efficacious one does the specific job it was given.

infallible vs. efficacious

infallible vs. efficacious: Infallible goes past efficacious — not just proven to work, but claimed never to fail at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — effic

Root — effic: to work out, accomplish (Latin ex- + facere, to make or do)

Suffix — -acious

Suffix — -acious: inclined to, full of

Put it together

Put it together: Effic- (to work out — Latin ex- + facere, "to make, to do") + -acious (full of) = full of the power to get a thing done. Latin efficax was the label for medicines and measures that delivered. The English word kept both the meaning and the courtroom tone: efficacious is what you call a remedy after it has proven itself.

Use the root in a new word: factory

Use the root in a new word: factory: The bicycle factory turns out three hundred frames a day.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / clinical

Efficacious is the lab-coat cousin of effective: reach for it when something has been tested against its intended result — remedies, policies, treatments — and passed. For people, use effective or capable; "an efficacious teacher" sounds like a dosage. And keep it clear of efficient, which measures how little a process wastes, not whether it works.
